findings.description: Unsafe XML parsing vulnerable to XXE (XML External Entity) attacks
findings.reasoning: The code uses xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring() to parse XML from an HTTP response without disabling external entity processing. The response comes from an S3 API call (response.text) which could be intercepted or manipulated. An attacker could inject XXE payloads in the XML response to read local files, perform SSRF attacks, or cause denial of service through billion laughs attacks. ElementTree is known to be vulnerable to XXE when external entities are not explicitly disabled.

evidence.code_context: XML parsing at line 292: err = ET.fromstring(message) where message comes from response.text (HTTP response from S3)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: response.text -> message -> ET.fromstring(message). Response data flows directly from HTTP response into XML parser without sanitization.
evidence.notes: ElementTree does not disable external entities by default. Should use defusedxml or configure parser to disable DTD/external entities.
